bg_facts: Hackers moved just over $6.3 billion out of Binance in about 20 minutes.
The FBI says North Korea was behind it.

slides.title: What *happened*
slides.body: Thursday at 4:05 PM Eastern, hackers got into Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange. In about 20 minutes they moved out just over $6.3 billion.

slides.title: Across *10 chains*
slides.body: Blockchain firm TRM Labs says the attacker ordered Binance's own wallets to empty into wallets the attacker controlled, on 10 different blockchains.

slides.title: How they *got in*
slides.body: Investigators say the hackers took over Binance's wallet signing system. Early findings suggest it began with one engineer's hacked laptop. Binance says it found no sign a private key leaked.

slides.title: Who did *it*
slides.body: The FBI confirmed on Saturday that North Korea was behind it. Experts point to a hacking unit in North Korea's military with a long record of crypto heists.

slides.title: The money *now*
slides.body: About $3 billion is frozen, including more than $2.3 billion frozen by Tether and Circle. Binance has not said what happened to the other $3.3 billion.

slides.title: What Binance *says*
slides.body: Binance says it will cover all losses and user funds are safe. Withdrawals were paused, aiming to resume in about 48 hours. Its $1 billion emergency fund is about one sixth of what was taken.

slides.title: What it means *for you*
slides.body: Crypto on an exchange is not insured like a bank deposit, so refunds are up to the exchange. Use app based two factor login, a unique password, and never keep everything on one exchange.
